title: Squared shear is not a heat-flux or reactor benefit
statement: Phase model predicts~1.87times expected local squared shear for a localized heat-loss region at unchanged amplitude, NOT1.87fold heat-flux reduction. Uniform temperature gradient, already optimal phase, unfavorable nonlinear energy supply, inadequate selectivity, detuning, diffusion, parasitic heating/transport or magnetic perturbations may erase benefit. Equally informed RF, neutral-beam and feedback control with same actuator may implement the same phase law or outperform it; no matched nonlinear confinement comparison completed. Needed joint interface: actual electromagnetic deposition map, complex naturally sustained mode response, resulting nonlinear heat flux. Existing field-line exit proof is a warning, not proof about this RF system;256case gyrokinetic dataset is potential calibration, not working-control evidence.

requires: Positive and negative absorbed-power profiles are independently programmable in a specified Gaussian deposition model; transfer efficiency, absorption, damping, diffusivity and width are inputs.
A turbulence-maintained mode U=A cos(kx-Omega t-theta) has a usable soft phase with acquired-in-model detuning, diffusion and force projection; this structure is not demonstrated for a reactor.

Turbulence-sustained amplitude, soft phase, programmable deposition, effective coupling and phase diffusion are supplied model inputs. Actual antenna-to-wave-to-mode susceptibility, transient dressing momentum, nonlinear heat-flux payoff and equally informed matched-control comparison remain unearned. costs: Both nonnegative wave powers, deposition selectivity, RF absorption, momentum transfer, transient stored dressing momentum and startup are paid.

Illustrative synthetic parameters and finite discretizations are not measured calibration, feasible antenna design or a full nonlinear gyrokinetic simulation; same actuator ordinary control remains a strong comparator.
